environment: Linux aarch64 disposable mount/net/PID namespaces; no physical router changes
scenario: Create six objects before service.set. On the same persistent provider connection, notify the sixth path immediately after set STATUS; inspect actual subscriber list and a distinct trigger output file. Repeat with fresh paths twelve times.
conclusion: The early-reply queue introduces a demonstrated R89 first-notification regression. C lacking this stronger return guarantee does not waive the regression.
fix: Hold one owned set/add request while attempting its service watches one per maintenance pass. Complete rc running and service.start only after attempts, then reply. Delay launching queued trigger commands until this boundary while maintaining running tasks. On transport failure preserve the local running hook, discard old-generation replies/events and owned request fds.

clean timeout finishes request and preserves background retry
partial-reply timeout drops owned request fd
